label: prop:neutron-prediction-comparison
title: Comparison of predicted and observed stable neutron numbers for $p \leq 103$
html:
At q = q_0, the beta-stability formula (beta-stability) fixes the beta-stability line p^*(A), the minimum-energy proton count at each mass number:

  p^*(A) =  \frac{A}{2 + c \cdot A^{2/3}},
  \qquad c = \frac{\lambda_C}{2a_{\mathrm{asym}}} = \frac{(q_0 - q_0^{-1})\,[6]_{q_0}}{6\,[2]_{q_0}[7]_{q_0}} \approx 0.01452,

with \lambda_C = (q - q^{-1})[6]_q\, m_e and a_{\mathrm{asym}} = 3[2]_q[7]_q\, m_e in balanced quantum integers, evaluated at the proton-pinned modulus q_0; the factor m_e cancels. The constant c is fixed by the q-integer coefficient assignments of Ch 11 §8, not derived: those assignments are stated, and nothing here derives the choice of [6]_q or 3[2]_q[7]_q.

The predicted neutron number at a given proton count is obtained by inverting that line: n_{\mathrm{pred}}(p) = A^*(p) - p, where A^* is the fixed point of A^* = p\left(2 + c\,{A^*}^{2/3}\right), rounded to the nearest integer. Compare n_{\mathrm{pred}} with the observed neutron number n_{\mathrm{obs}}(p) across 103 elements, where n_{\mathrm{obs}}(p) is the neutron number of the most abundant naturally occurring isotope (NUBASE2020), or of the longest-lived ground state for an element with no naturally occurring isotope:

See Table.

The mean discrepancy is \overline{|\Delta n|} \approx 1.82. The maximum discrepancy |\Delta n| = 7 occurs at p = 52 (tellurium, whose most abundant isotope {}^{130}\mathrm{Te} lies far on the neutron-rich side).
